release_decision.reason: Independent review still finds unresolved canonical identity collisions, a sequence under-splitting, five target-type errors, and two direct major-direction errors. The 115-target denominator is retained and is not lowered to make the totals look complete.
blocking_conditions: Split the three cross-page canonical collisions without merging distinct official identities.
Preserve distinct identities for the Coursera Algorithms I & II sequence.
Repair the five false course_sequence classifications and the two LLM/NLP major-direction classifications.
Keep the 115 registry target denominator until identity repairs are applied; do not silently discard targets.

offline_only.source_of_authority: Only the pinned snapshot, current registry, and current discovery script were inspected. Older audit reports were not used as authority.

method.nav_enumeration: Independently parsed the pinned mkdocs nav leaves, resolved every Markdown path inside the snapshot, counted unique source paths, and compared the resulting leaf keys with the registry.
method.target_enumeration: Independently grouped official course identity evidence from nav title, guide heading, course-introduction text, institution, explicit course numbers, and source path. Same-page translation/title aliases were not treated as new identities; distinct official numbers and distinct cross-page course pages were not collapsed.
method.target_type_rule: A course_sequence requires source evidence of paired/sequential official identities. A slash, ampersand, or duplicate formatting of one course number is not sufficient by itself.
method.direction_rule: Navigation category is primary evidence; substantive guide title/body can refine a broad category. Neural-network wording is not computer-network evidence. Numerical analysis is numerical_scientific_computing.
method.reason_completeness_rule: A classification reason must explain the observed type and, for a sequence, identify the sequence or paired official identities; a generic course-like sentence plus identifiers is insufficient for sequence pages.

structural_findings.source_evidence: Independent walk of mkdocs.yml produces 135 Markdown nav leaves, 135 unique source paths, zero duplicate nav occurrences, and zero missing files.
structural_findings.independent_conclusion: Nav and source counts match; the 23 non-course leaves remain explicitly represented.

structural_findings.source_evidence: Independent source review expects 105 course leaves and 7 true sequence leaves. The seven sequence pages are MITmaths.md, CS149.md, Algo.md, CMU10-414.md, CMU15-442.md, EE16.md, and CS106B_CS106X.md.
structural_findings.registry_evidence: Registry records 100 course leaves and 12 course_sequence leaves. The five excess sequence classifications are CSAPP.md, CS571.md, MIT6-7960.md, EECS498-007.md, and CS229M.md.
structural_findings.independent_conclusion: The nav/source denominator is intact, but the target_type projection is not release-safe.

structural_findings.source_evidence: The three collision groups contain six distinct source identity keys: two separate PKU guide pages, two separate NJU guide pages, and the unrelated AICS and LHY guide pages. Their titles, institutions, nav categories, and guide bodies are distinct.
structural_findings.registry_evidence: course_targets groups both PKU pages under pku-pku, both NJU pages under nju-nju, and AICS.md plus LHY.md under unknown. The registry still reports 115 canonical targets.
structural_findings.independent_conclusion: 115 is retained as the current denominator, but the independently proven distinct-identity lower bound is 115 - 3 merged target slots + 6 source identities = 118. The collisions block release and must not be repaired by reducing the denominator.

structural_findings.source_evidence: The snapshot has 135 unique nav source paths and no duplicate path occurrence. Same-page title/heading and numeric-format aliases are legitimate alias evidence, while PKU, NJU, AICS, and LHY are different source pages with different official course subjects.
structural_findings.registry_evidence: language_variants are single-language for all 115 targets, but guide_page_provenance has three multi-page target groups: nju-nju, pku-pku, and unknown. Their aliases are different titles rather than translations of one official identity.
structural_findings.independent_conclusion: No translation-only merge was found; however, the alias/canonicalization result still collapses distinct official identities across pages, so the identity gate remains blocked.

structural_findings.source_evidence: Seven source pages explicitly describe paired or multi-course identities: MIT18.01/18.02, CMU15-418/Stanford CS149, Coursera Algorithms I & II, CMU10-414/714, CMU15-442/642, EE16A&B, and Stanford CS106B/X.
structural_findings.registry_evidence: Each affected leaf has a generic reason such as 'course-like instructional content' plus identifiers, but does not state why it is a sequence or how distinct official identities are preserved. Seven leaves therefore fail the reason-completeness check.
structural_findings.independent_conclusion: Classification reasons are present for all 135 leaves, but seven sequence reasons are not complete enough for independent review.

structural_findings.source_evidence: Category-first review confirms CS168 networks, numerical analysis numerical_scientific_computing, and neural-network pages without computer-networks evidence. Separate LLM/NLP pages are under the large-language-model category and describe LLM/NLP content, while merged NJU/PKU pages carry conflicting category evidence.
structural_findings.registry_evidence: CS168, MIT18.330, and the two neural pages now carry the corrected direction evidence. CMU11-667 and CMU11-711 remain other_computing with 'no substantive direction marker matched'; nju-nju and pku-pku retain a single compilers direction after merging programming-language pages with compiler pages.
structural_findings.independent_conclusion: The three newly specified direction rules pass, but two direct LLM/NLP direction errors and two collision-induced ambiguous targets remain.

structural_findings.source_evidence: A fresh offline invocation of the current script reproduces 135 nav leaves, 112 course leaves, 115 targets, and the same 100/12 course/course_sequence split. Source pages show that several slash/ampersand forms are cross-listed aliases or one-course numeric formats.
structural_findings.registry_evidence: scripts/discover_csdiy_courses.py:676 classifies any len(codes)>1 or title marker '/', '&', 'sequence', etc. as course_sequence. Lines 365-368 expand numeric slash forms, while lines 207-209 later normalize CMU CS15213 to 15-213; the sequence decision precedes that canonical equivalence. Lines 192-196 remove Chinese characters and return unknown when no Latin slug remains; lines 481-489 then use institution-title slugs, producing pku-pku, nju-nju, and unknown collisions.
structural_findings.independent_conclusion: The current deterministic script reproduces the registry's structural counts but still contains the identity and sequence heuristics responsible for the blocked findings.
